findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Clients scopes/resources
findings.body: init() returns as soon as realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null. Realms that already had the V2 admin-permissions client before this change will therefore never get the newly added Clients scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) or the 'Clients' all-resource. Creating a client permission later fails in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource when those new scopes are not found ('No scopes found.'), and ClientPermissionsV2 can then fall back to a null resource and NPE in policyStore.findByResource. Initialization needs to be idempotent and upgrade an existing admin-permissions resource server by adding missing scopes/resources.

findings.title: Client-specific resources are looked up with the wrong owner id
findings.body: The third argument to ResourceStore.findByName is the resource owner. V2 per-resource authorization resources are created with owner resourceServer.getClientId() in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (line 104), but this lookup passes server.getId(), which is the Keycloak client UUID (see AdminPermissionsSchema.isAdminPermissionClient). The lookup therefore misses the per-client resource and falls back to the 'Clients' all-resource, ignoring per-client grants/denials: per-client MANAGE/VIEW grants do not work, and a per-client negative permission can be bypassed by a global allow. The same owner mistake exists at line 244 for the 'Clients' all-resource lookup. Use the same owner as creation or the two-argument findByName.

findings.title: Client removal event breaks when V2 permissions are enabled
findings.body: The new listener guard checks only Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled, ClientRemovedEvent reaches clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...), which ClientPermissionsV2 overrides to throw UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client can fail. If only V2 is enabled, the listener is skipped entirely and the deleted client's V2 permission resource/policies are never cleaned up. The guard needs to handle V2 explicitly (skip it or provide a no-op/cleanup implementation).

findings.title: canExchangeTo now throws UnsupportedOperationException under V2
findings.body: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException. Token exchange invokes this evaluator, so token exchange requests will return a 500 instead of a normal authorization decision. Implement the check or return a denial; the other overrides that throw UnsupportedOperationException are similarly reachable from management endpoints and should not leak 500s.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the new Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases USERS. For the newly added CLIENTS resource type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for resources created by getOrCreateResource. Client permission resources will therefore be shown with null/empty names instead of the client id or 'All clients' in APIs/UI. Add a CLIENTS branch analogous to the USERS branch.

findings.title: requireView/requireViewClientScopes Javadoc incorrectly describes return values
findings.body: The Javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The same wrong text is repeated for requireViewClientScopes() at line 101. This contradicts the actual contract and will mislead implementors; document both as throwing ForbiddenException when the corresponding can* check is false.
